analysis:
Examined ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.swift (head text, lines 1-671) and the ClusterSetupWizardLiveOperations.swift patch (servingScope setting, coordinator flag on plan(), discovery-mode selection).

ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts (v1 to v2 schema): the canonical parser is strict. It requires the exact field set at every level, checks for repeated keys (repeatsAKey), caps size at 64KiB, and requires 64-hex nonzero digests. It also bounds models (1..64, sorted, unique) and mode families (known, sorted, unique). Parity qualifications are checked for schedule 1/2, per-member numerics classes, positive ascending cuts, never promotable and diverged together, an RFC3339 qualified_at, token bounds, video only with vision, and no repeated placement. Derived IDs are capped at 128 bytes. The facts are computed from files after realpath resolution, hashed with DistributedInstalledFiles.digest, and the worker is pinned by --expected-executable-sha256. Describe also rejects capabilities that report private images. The facts approve nothing by themselves; a coordinator or release lane has to consume them. Declared public models (ClusterPublicModels.declared) get a hardcoded grant and parity qualification keyed on runtimeModelID, catalog ID and artifact hash, so the declaration is bound to the described artifact. The catalog input_modalities file is read with a 4096-byte bound and strict keys. Residual questions I did not verify: the coordinator side (platform-owned) that turns these facts into grants and qualifications, and whether the release lane takes the facts from the final signed app. Also unverified: the realpath-to-use TOCTOU window between hashing and execution, which is the same pattern as the existing installed-file checks and is outside the supplied evidence. No threat-model assets in the provider consumed-authorization scope (TB-011, T-054) appear weakened; the change touches cluster config rather than App Attest authorization.

ClusterSetupWizardLiveOperations: the change adds an optional servingScope and a coordinator flag to plan(), and swaps mtpMode for a discovery mode via ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.discoveryMode(mtpMode, coordinator:). For coordinator serving it drops the speculative assistant under auto, which narrows rather than widens the surface. The implementation of discoveryMode is not supplied, so I could not confirm it never enables more than the configured mtpMode. This is low risk and is noted as a remaining integration question.

No concrete security regression identified in the supplied units.
